q: Does TSH rising with normal aging indicate occult thyroid failure?
o: Yes - normal aging necessarily lowers free T4
Yes - rising TSH with stable free T4 proves occult failure
No - TSH cannot increase in people without thyroid disease
No - free T4 remains unchanged in euthyroid aging
explanation:
TSH gradually rises with normal aging without a fall in free T4 in euthyroid people without thyroid disease; this does not indicate occult failure (p1546).

A. Yes - normal aging necessarily lowers free T4: The text describes unchanged free T4 in euthyroid aging (p1546).
C. No - TSH cannot increase in people without thyroid disease: TSH gradually increases even without underlying thyroid disease or autoimmunity (p1546).
B. Yes - rising TSH with stable free T4 proves occult failure: The book explicitly says this normal-aging pattern does not indicate occult failure (p1546).

q: A patient on 112 μg levothyroxine daily has a rising TSH. Before assuming disease progression, what simple explanation should be checked?
o: An unchanged average dose despite missing a weekly tablet
Absence of a TSH response to missed replacement doses
Missed doses and difficulty with adherence
Increased exposure from missing a weekly tablet
explanation:
Adherence should be considered first when TSH varies; missing one weekly dose of 112 micrograms reduces the daily average to 96 micrograms (p1552).

A. An unchanged average dose despite missing a weekly tablet: The prescribed 112-microgram dose does not ensure the delivered average if doses are missed (p1552).
D. Increased exposure from missing a weekly tablet: The example lowers the average from 112 to 96 micrograms (p1552).
B. Absence of a TSH response to missed replacement doses: The text discusses TSH elevation after stabilization and checking adherence and interacting conditions (p1552).

q: In managing myxedema coma, what is the critical sequencing error to avoid regarding hydrocortisone and thyroid hormone?
o: Initiating hydrocortisone to cover potentially impaired adrenal reserve
Giving thyroid hormone without hydrocortisone when adrenal reserve is impaired
Obtaining serum for cortisol measurement before starting hydrocortisone
Stopping hydrocortisone after the cortisol level is found adequate
explanation:
Thyroid hormone without hydrocortisone can precipitate adrenal crisis when adrenal reserve is impaired in myxedema coma (p1553).

C. Obtaining serum for cortisol measurement before starting hydrocortisone: The book recommends obtaining serum and then initiating IV hydrocortisone (p1553).
A. Initiating hydrocortisone to cover potentially impaired adrenal reserve: This is the recommended protection against adrenal crisis (p1553).
D. Stopping hydrocortisone after the cortisol level is found adequate: The book permits stopping it once cortisol is found adequate (p1553).
